correctness.rationale: The block operator has norm \(2\) and a nonzero kernel; the orbit identity \(T\Theta_k=\Theta_{k+1}\) holds for every integer index. The negative and positive geometric-series contributions are \(4/3\) and \(1/3\), giving tight bound \(5/3\). Orthogonal negative-index ranges force infinite-dimensional operator span, while \(\Theta_2=\Theta_1/2\) is an explicit dependence. For the repair, any finite dependence gives a finite forward-invariant span; injectivity on the algebraic range span allows the relation to be propagated backward, forcing the whole bi-infinite orbit into a finite-dimensional space and contradicting the hypothesis.

final_claim: There is a tight \(g\)-fusion frame with a bounded noninjective representing operator, infinite-dimensional operator span, and an explicit dependence \(\Theta_2=\Theta_1/2\), so Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.3(ii) of arXiv:2305.08182v1 are false as stated; injectivity of the representing operator on \(\operatorname{span}\{M_k\}\) suffices to restore the Proposition 4.1 conclusion.
